transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... honestly, I am just so, so tired. It’s not like a normal kind of tired, you know? I work as a cashier, and usually I can handle being on my feet all day, scanning items, dealing with the long lines and the customers, but lately... I mean, I can barely get through a single shift. It’s taking everything out of me just to stand there. 

It literally feels like my whole body is just filled with wet sand. Every time I try to lift my arms to bag something or just shift my weight at the register, it's so heavy and dragging. And the worst part is, I’ll go home after work and just completely collapse. I'll lay in bed for hours, thinking if I just sleep enough I'll finally feel better, but resting doesn’t really bring me back. I wake up and that wet sand feeling is still right there. My manager is even starting to notice how slow I'm moving, and I try to push through it, I really do, but no matter how much I sit down or try to catch my breath on my breaks, this deep exhaustion just stays stuck in my bones. I just don't know how to shake it off, and it's making every single day feel impossible.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

I don't know if "sad" is really the right word for it. Like, when I think of being sad, I think of crying over a movie or, you know, feeling heartbroken about something specific happening. But I haven't really been crying at all. It's more like... I just don't feel much of anything because I'm so incredibly drained. 

I'll be lying there in my room—I have this little TV set up at the foot of my bed, and usually I love watching those home renovation shows, you know, the ones where they flip the houses in a week? I usually get so into them, but lately I just leave it on for background noise. I'm not sitting there weeping or feeling sorry for myself, I'm just staring at the screen, totally blank. 

My sister called me the other day to ask if I was upset about something because I haven't been answering her texts, and I tried to explain to her that I'm not sitting around crying, I just literally don't have the energy to pick up the phone and type out a response. So I wouldn't really say I'm sad, exactly. Just... flattened out, I guess? Like everything is just too much effort, and even having feelings takes too much energy right now. Does that make sense? Because I keep trying to sit there and figure out if I'm actually sad, but it really just always comes back to that heavy, exhausted feeling I was just talking about.
Have you lost interest in activities you normally enjoy?

Yeah, actually, that’s... that’s a really big part of it. Like I was saying about the TV shows, it’s not just that. It’s everything. Things I usually love doing just... they just feel completely flat now. 

Like, usually, I really enjoy cooking for myself. I’d come home from the grocery store and put on some music and chop up vegetables and take my time trying a new recipe, you know? It was my way to unwind after dealing with people at the register all day. But now, I just open the fridge, look at the food, and I just can't bring myself to care. I just close the door and go back to bed. 

And my guitar, too. I've played acoustic guitar since high school, and usually, if I'm stressed, I'll just sit on the edge of my bed and play for an hour. But it's just been sitting in the corner of my room gathering dust. I actually picked it up the other day because I thought, you know, maybe this will help me snap out of it, but... I just strummed a few chords and put it right back down. It felt like I was only pretending to care. 

It’s the exact same with hiking. There's this beautiful trail I usually hike on my days off, and I haven't been out there in weeks. Even going over to my family’s place... we usually do these big Sunday get-togethers, and I used to look forward to them all week. I love my family, I really do. But now, if I even manage to drag myself over there, I'm just sitting at the table going through the motions. I'll smile and nod when my mom talks to me, and I'll pass the food around, but inside, I'm just totally blank. It really does feel like I'm just an actor putting on a show, pretending to be interested in my own life. I just don't get any spark or joy out of any of those things anymore, no matter how hard I try to force it.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite lately?

Well, yeah, it's... it's been really weird, honestly. My appetite has just been completely all over the place. Like, there were a few days a while back where I was just eating everything in sight, but lately... mostly I just completely forget to eat. 

It's like I was saying about cooking, right? I used to love making these big, complicated meals, like this lemon herb chicken I make, or these roasted root vegetables... I'd spend an hour chopping and seasoning and getting everything just perfect. But now, even if I do manage to force myself to make something simple, like just toast or maybe a bowl of cereal, it literally just tastes like cardboard. I'll put a bite in my mouth and I'm just chewing and chewing, and there's no flavor, no enjoyment, nothing. It's just a chore. 

And because of that, I've just been skipping meals left and right. I'll go a whole shift at the register and realize on my drive home that I haven't eaten anything since the day before. And it's definitely starting to show, too. I wear these black slacks for work—they have this specific uniform policy, you know, black pants, polo shirt—and I've had the same three pairs of pants for a couple of years now. They used to fit perfectly, maybe even a little snug after the holidays, but the last couple of weeks, I've been having to pull my belt tighter and tighter. They're just hanging off me now, really loose around the waist and the thighs. 

My mom actually pointed it out at that Sunday dinner I mentioned. She was trying to push a second helping of pot roast on me, saying I looked like I was wasting away, which, you know, she always exaggerates, but... she wasn't entirely wrong. I just can't bring myself to care about food right now. It's just too much effort to figure out what to eat, make it, and then force it down when it all tastes like nothing anyway.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Sleep? Oh, gosh, sleep has been a total nightmare lately. Well, not literal nightmares, but just... the whole process of trying to sleep. It's completely messed up. 

It kind of started with my schedule at work. Being a cashier, they really bounce you around. One week you're on opening shift, which means I have to be there at 5:30 in the morning to count the drawer before the doors open at 6:00, and then the next week they'll have me closing, so I don't get out until after 11:00 at night. And then sometimes they do these horrible "clopens" where you close one night and open the next morning, which I don't even think should be legal, but they do it anyway. 

So with all those changing shifts, my body clock just got completely thrown off. There was a stretch a little while ago where I would get home from a closing shift, and I'd only sleep for maybe two or three hours, but I'd wake up feeling completely wired. Like, I didn't even need the sleep. I'd just be buzzing, ready to go, like I drank a pot of coffee, even though I hadn't. I'd just get up and start cleaning my apartment or reorganizing my closet at 3:00 in the morning because I just had all this energy and I couldn't just lay there in the dark. 

But now... now it's different. Now I have that heavy, exhausted feeling I was telling you about earlier, where just existing takes too much effort. I am so tired all the time. My bones feel tired. But even when I'm that exhausted, and I finally manage to drag myself into bed, I can't stay asleep. I'll fall asleep okay, usually, because I'm just so drained, but then I'll wake up at, like, 4:00 in the morning, hours before my alarm is supposed to go off. And the worst part is, as soon as my eyes open, my mind is already going. It's just racing, but not with good things or energetic things like before. Just... spinning. And I'll just lie there in the dark, staring at the ceiling, feeling so unbelievably tired but completely unable to drift back off. So I just lay there for hours, exhausted, until I finally have to get up for work. It's like my brain forgot how to actually rest.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything lately?

Guilty? Yeah... gosh, yeah. It's actually really overwhelming, to be honest. I just keep thinking about how I'm letting absolutely everybody down right now. It's like this constant, miserable loop in my head. 

Like at work, my manager—her name is Brenda—she's usually pretty strict but she's been trying to be patient with me, but I just know I'm a massive burden to her and the whole team right now. I'm moving so slow, and I just... I replay every single mistake I make at the cash register. Like the other day, I accidentally double-scanned a carton of eggs, and I didn't even notice until the customer pointed it out, and I had to call Brenda over with her key to void it. It was such a small thing, took maybe two minutes to fix, but I just kept replaying it the rest of my shift, and the whole drive home, and then while I was lying awake in bed staring at the ceiling. It just loops and loops in my brain, like it's this absolute proof that I’m just... I’m no good. Like I can't even do a basic job right anymore. 

And then it spills over into my family, too. Like those Sunday dinners I was telling you about. I'm letting them down just by being there and being so blank and miserable. Especially my little nieces. They're four and six, and they always run up to me wanting to play, you know, wanting me to get down on the rug and do puzzles or play pretend with their dolls. And I just can't do it. I just sit on the couch like a lump and tell them I'm too tired. They look so confused and disappointed, and I just feel this crushing guilt about it. I'm supposed to be the fun aunt. I used to be! But now I'm just ruining their afternoon, and I'm ruining my mom's dinner by not eating, and I'm messing up at the store... I just feel like I'm a giant disappointment to everyone who has to interact with me. It’s just this heavy, awful feeling that I owe everyone an apology just for being around them.
How long have you been feeling this way?

How long? Gosh, um... time is just such a blur right now, to be completely honest with you. It feels like I've been stuck in this quicksand forever, but if I really sit down and try to map it out, try to put an actual timeline on it... I'd say this really low, empty part has lasted for about four months now. 

Yeah, four months. Because, you know, I was telling you about that time when I was bouncing off the walls, surviving on two hours of sleep and reorganizing my closet at three in the morning? That first rush of energy at work with the schedule changes... well, this heavy feeling started long after that passed. 

I actually remember exactly when it really hit me, because it was right around the time the store started putting out all the seasonal displays. We were getting all the autumn stuff in, all the pumpkin spice endcaps and the early Halloween candy, which is always just a massive headache to set up. Brenda had me on inventory for it, and I just remember standing there in aisle four, holding this heavy cardboard box of plastic spiders, and just feeling this... this absolute wave of nothingness wash over me. Like someone just completely pulled the plug on my battery, you know? 

And that was, what, four months ago? Yeah. And ever since that day with the boxes in aisle four, it's just been this constant, dragging weight. Every single day for four months, just waking up at 4:00 AM, feeling completely empty, dreading going in to the register, dreading sitting on the couch at my mom's house... it just hasn't lifted at all. It's just been four straight months of feeling totally hollowed out.
Have you been having any thoughts about hurting yourself or wishing you weren't alive?

Hurting myself? Um... gosh, that's a really hard thing to say out loud. But... yeah. I have been having these really scary thoughts lately. It's not like I'm sitting around making a detailed plan or anything, but it goes right back to that massive guilt I was just talking about. When I'm lying there at 4:00 in the morning, just staring at the dark ceiling while my mind spins, my brain just starts telling me that everyone would honestly be so much better off if I just... didn't wake up. Like, if I could just finally go to sleep and stay asleep forever, then Brenda wouldn't have to deal with my stupid mistakes at the register, and my mom wouldn't have to worry about me not eating, and my nieces wouldn't have to see their aunt acting like a miserable zombie. It just feels like I'm taking up space and making everyone miserable, and it would just be so much easier for all of them if I wasn't here to be a burden anymore. 

And it's not just when I'm in bed, either, which is what really scares me. Like, I take the bus home from the store, so I have to walk a few blocks down the main road after my shifts. And a few times recently, on the way home, especially after those really long shifts where my bones are just aching and I feel so incredibly empty... I'll be standing there at the intersection waiting for the walk signal, watching all the cars zoom by, and I've caught myself actually thinking about just... taking one step off the curb. Just stepping right out into the traffic. Just letting a car hit me so I wouldn't have to feel this heavy, awful dragging weight for one more second. It's usually just a split-second thought, and I always step back from the edge of the sidewalk, but it absolutely terrifies me that my brain even goes there. I don't want to do that, I really don't, but the thoughts just sneak up on me and they get so loud, and I'm just so, so tired of fighting them.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

Moving slowly? Oh, absolutely. It's like... it's like I'm moving through molasses, or like I'm wearing a lead suit or something. Everything just takes so much effort now. 

It's actually really weird, because if you think back to when I was talking about that time a few months ago when I was just buzzing with energy... back then, I couldn't sit still if my life depended on it. I was constantly pacing up and down the aisles at work, straightening every single candy bar, facing all the cans so the labels were perfectly aligned, just speed-walking everywhere. Brenda actually told me I was making her dizzy. I was just go, go, go, talking a mile a minute, bouncing on my heels behind the register. 

But now? Now it's the exact opposite. It's like that battery didn't just drain, it completely died and started rusting. Just walking from the breakroom to my register feels like a marathon. My legs feel so heavy, like I have to actively tell my brain to pick up my feet and put them down again. And it's not just walking, either. It's... it's everything. Even just talking. Like, when a customer asks me a question, like where the baking soda is, it feels like there's this huge delay between them speaking, me understanding the words, and then me actually getting my mouth to form an answer. It's like my brain is wading through thick mud just to say "aisle six." I can see them looking at me, waiting for me to respond, and I know I should be answering faster, but I just... I can't. The words just drag out of me. 

And the walk to the bus stop after my shift? Gosh, it used to take me maybe ten minutes, tops. Now I feel like I'm shuffling the whole way there. I have to stop and catch my breath, not because I'm out of shape, but just because my body feels so incredibly heavy and slow. It's just exhausting, having to force myself through every single movement all day long.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

Enjoy? Pleasure? Honestly, no. Not at all. And that's... that's been one of the hardest parts of this whole thing, to be perfectly honest with you. It's like someone came in and just painted over my entire life in gray. 

I used to have all these things I really loved doing, things that made me feel like *me*, you know? Like, I've played guitar since I was a teenager. Nothing fancy, just acoustic, mostly folk stuff, but I used to love sitting on my bed after a long shift at the store and just strumming for an hour. It would completely unwind me. I had this whole routine where I'd make a cup of chamomile tea, tune my guitar, and just play whatever came to mind. But now? My guitar has just been sitting in its case in the corner of my room for months. I look at it and I just feel... nothing. I don't even have the desire to open the case. 

And cooking! Oh my gosh, I used to love cooking for myself. I'd go to the farmer's market on my days off, pick out fresh vegetables, look up new recipes online... I made this amazing roasted butternut squash risotto last fall that I was so proud of. But now, the thought of standing in the kitchen, chopping vegetables, standing over a hot stove... it's just exhausting, and honestly, food doesn't even taste good anymore. It's all just cardboard. I've basically been surviving on plain toast and microwave oatmeal because I just don't care.

Even getting outside used to be a big thing for me. I used to go hiking on the weekends at the state park just outside of town. I loved the smell of the pine trees and the feeling of the dirt under my boots. I had this favorite trail that went up to a little waterfall... but I haven't been out there since the summer. The idea of putting on my hiking boots and driving out there just feels completely pointless. 

And my family... I mentioned my nieces earlier. I usually love going over to my sister's place, or my mom's, for Sunday dinners. I used to be the fun aunt, you know? Playing board games with the girls, helping them build pillow forts, laughing until my sides hurt. But now, when I go over there, I just sit on the couch like a lump. I watch them playing, and I know I *should* feel happy, I know I *should* want to join in, but I just feel completely flat. It's like I'm an alien observing them from behind a glass wall. I try to smile and nod and ask them about school, but I'm really just pretending to care. It's all just an act, a really exhausting performance, because inside, I just feel totally dead to it all. It's like every single thing that used to bring me a tiny spark of joy has just been completely snuffed out.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your physical activity level or movements over the past four months?

Yeah, I mean, I know I kind of touched on this just a little bit ago when you asked about me moving slow, but if we're looking at the whole picture of the last four months... it's just been this massive, unbelievable rollercoaster with how my body actually moves. 

Like, if you go back to a few months ago, at first, I absolutely could not stop pacing around the store. It was like I had this motor inside me that just wouldn't shut off, no matter what I did. I'd be at work, and I'd just be doing laps around the registers, darting down the aisles, straightening every single little item. I'd spend what felt like hours just making sure all the chapsticks and the gum wrappers were facing the exact same direction, and I was moving so incredibly fast, just buzzing around the place. I couldn't have sat in a chair if you paid me to. 

But then, over the last couple of months, it's just... it's completely flipped. Lately, it's exactly what I was trying to describe earlier. Everything is just so incredibly slowed down and heavy now. It's not just that I'm tired, it's like my actual limbs are made of concrete. Even just the most basic, everyday stuff, like walking out to the bus stop after my shift, or even just opening my mouth to physically form the words to answer a question from a customer... it takes everything I have. It feels like I'm dragging a hundred pounds of rocks with me everywhere I go. It's like my physical body just completely burned out from all that pacing I did back then, and now it just refuses to work at a normal speed.
Have you experienced any periods where you felt like you were moving or talking faster than usual?

Yeah, I mean, I know I brought up the pacing earlier, but the talking... oh my gosh, yes. It was like my mouth was just desperately trying to keep up with my brain, and it could barely even do that. Back during that same time, a few months ago when I was just buzzing around the store, I was talking an absolute mile a minute. 

I remember people at work, my coworkers and even the shift leads, they kept telling me to just take a breath and slow down. I would corner them in the breakroom or when we were standing behind the registers and I would just start going off about the shift schedules, or how we desperately needed to overhaul the entire inventory system in the stockroom because the way they had it set up was just completely inefficient. I had all these massive ideas for the supervisors about how to run the store better, how we could reorganize the endcaps and manage the checkout lines to maximize flow, and I would just be rapid-firing all this information at them. 

I would be explaining my whole intricate plan, going into all these little details about barcode scanners and overlapping shifts, and I would look at their faces and I could just clearly see that they weren't following me at all. Their eyes would sort of glaze over, and they'd look so confused, just completely lost, because the words were pouring out of me so incredibly fast that they couldn't even process what I was saying. I just had so much to say and it all felt so important and urgent, you know? Like if I didn't get every single thought out right that exact second, I was going to explode. So I would just talk and talk and talk, and they would just stand there holding up their hands, telling me I needed to slow down because they couldn't understand a single thing I was throwing at them.
Have there been any times over the past four months when you felt slightly more interested in the things you used to enjoy?

No... no, not even a little bit. I know people say feeling down comes in waves, or that you're supposed to have good days and bad days, but for me, it's just been this one long, flat, gray line. Like I was saying about the guitar and the cooking and going over to my sister's place... I keep waiting for even just a tiny spark, you know? Like maybe I'll wake up one Tuesday and think, "Hey, maybe I'll go look at the vegetables at the market today," or "Maybe I'll just strum one chord." But it never happens. 

It's just been this constant, heavy emptiness. And this low, empty part, it has lasted about four months now. Just four solid months of absolutely nothing. It set in long after that first rush of energy at work passed—you know, that time I was telling you about where I was pacing the aisles and trying to overhaul the inventory and talking everyone's ear off? Once all that buzzing and rushing around finally burned out, it was like hitting a brick wall. And ever since I hit that wall, for these entire four months, there hasn't been a single break in the emptiness. Not one afternoon where I felt even slightly interested in my old life. It's just... I'm just dragging myself through my shifts at the register and then staring at the wall in my bedroom, every single day, for four months straight.
Have you felt like your condition has significantly impacted your ability to function at work or in your personal relationships?

Oh, absolutely. I mean, it's just completely derailed everything, to be honest with you. At work... well, at work it's just been a disaster lately. I was trying so hard to keep it together, you know, because I actually really wanted to move up. I had my eye on this shift lead position, and I thought if I just worked hard and showed them I could handle the extra responsibility, they'd consider me. But then everything just got so heavy and slow, like I was telling you before. My brain just feels like sludge now. 

I started making all these stupid mistakes at the register. Just dumb things, like giving the wrong change, or scanning things twice and not catching it, or completely forgetting how to process a basic return. And the cash-office tasks... I used to be able to balance a drawer in my sleep, but lately, I'd just sit back there staring at the screen, and the numbers wouldn't even make sense anymore. I was falling so far behind on everything. And then my manager, she finally pulled me aside into the little office in the back, and she just took me off all those extra responsibilities. She said I needed to "focus on the basics" right now, which is just manager-speak for "you're messing up too much." So there goes any chance I had of getting promoted anytime soon. It was just so humiliating, sitting in that tiny office and having her take all that away from me when I had been trying so hard.

And it's not just work, it's... it's my personal life, too. I've completely isolated myself. I've been avoiding my family entirely. My sister keeps texting me, asking if I want to come over for dinner or if I want to see my niece, and I just... I can't. I can't even bring myself to reply to her most of the time. I just leave my phone on silent and let the messages pile up. I don't want them to see me like this, just this empty shell of a person dragging myself around. And it got so bad... I mean, it got so overwhelmingly dark and heavy the other day that I actually had to call for same-day crisis help. I just... I was sitting on my bedroom floor, and I realized I didn't feel safe being by myself anymore. I couldn't handle the weight of it alone for one more second. I just felt like I was going to completely break apart if I didn't get someone to help me right then and there. So, yeah, it's... it's definitely impacting every single part of my life. It feels like everything is just falling apart.
Have you ever thought about how you would hurt yourself if you were to act on those thoughts of not wanting to be alive?

Well, I mean... it's hard to even say out loud, honestly, because it just sounds so awful when you actually put words to it. But, yeah, I have. I've had these really, really scary thoughts lately. It usually starts when I'm just lying there in bed, staring at the ceiling, and my brain just starts telling me that everyone would be so much better off if I just didn't wake up the next day. Like, if I could just go to sleep and that would be the end of it, you know? It wouldn't be this huge burden on my sister anymore, and my manager wouldn't have to deal with me messing up the cash drawer, and I wouldn't have to feel this... this crushing weight every single second of the day. 

And then... well, then it kind of spills over into when I'm actually out of the house. Like, a few times recently, when I was walking home from my shift... I take this one route that goes past the big intersection near the grocery store, the one where the cars are always flying by way over the speed limit because the light stays green for so long. And I've caught myself, more than once, just standing there on the edge of the sidewalk, looking at the cars rushing past, and thinking about just... just stepping off the curb right into the traffic. Just one step, and it would all be over. I wouldn't have to think anymore, I wouldn't have to feel this empty anymore. 

It's terrifying, really, because in that split second, it almost feels like it makes sense. Like it would be a relief. And then I snap out of it and realize what I was just thinking, and my heart starts pounding out of my chest, and I have to practically run the rest of the way home because I'm so scared of my own brain. It's just... it's like this dark cloud that follows me around, constantly whispering these terrible things, and sometimes I feel like I'm barely holding on against it.
Have you had any days or periods over the last four months where you felt even slightly better than you do now?

No... no, I really haven't. I mean, I try to think back, you know? I look at the calendar and I realize it's been four whole months, which just sounds insane when I actually say it out loud... because honestly, sometimes it just feels like one incredibly long, never-ending day. But no, there hasn't been a single day where I woke up and thought, "Oh, okay, the air feels a little lighter today." 

I keep waiting for it, I really do. I'll lay there in the morning, just staring at the ceiling, listening to the cars outside or the people in the apartment upstairs walking around, and I'll do this sort of... mental check, I guess? Like, "Am I okay today? Is the sludge gone? Can I finally text my sister back?" And every single time, without fail, the answer is just... no. It's just this heavy, suffocating blanket that never, ever lifts. Not even for an hour. 

I mean, you'd think just by pure chance, right? Just by the law of averages, you'd have one afternoon where the weather is nice, or maybe a customer at the register is actually polite to you for once, and you'd feel a little bit of a lift. Like, just a fraction of a percent better. But it doesn't happen. The customers come and go, my shifts start and end, the sun comes up and goes down, and I'm just trapped in the exact same miserable, empty spot. It's like I'm stuck in amber or something. Just frozen in this awful, heavy state. So, no... no breaks. No good days. Just the exact same dark feeling, day in and day out, without any letup at all.
Have you experienced any hallucinations or delusions during these four months?

Well, during these last four months? No. Not during this... this awful, heavy period. But... well, right before this all started, there was this stretch of time. You know how I mentioned earlier that I was trying to get that shift lead position and showing them I could handle extra responsibility? Well, there was this time right before the crash where I was just... I was so incredibly wired. It was like someone had plugged my brain straight into a wall socket, and I was just buzzing constantly. I was barely sleeping at all—I mean, maybe an hour or two a night, if that—and I'd just spring out of bed feeling completely energized, like I didn't even need rest. 

I was taking on way too much at work, volunteering for extra shifts, doing everybody else's tasks on top of mine, just running around the store because my mind was speeding so fast. I couldn't slow my thoughts down, I had all these ideas about how to reorganize the entire front end of the store and how I could fix everything. 

And that's... that's when the whispering started. It was just these whispering voices. I'd be standing there in the breakroom, or sweeping the aisles after closing, and I'd hear them, like there were people just right over my shoulder murmuring to each other. It really freaked me out at first because I had never, ever heard anything like that before in my entire life. It was completely new. But it only happened during that specific wired stretch when I was going a million miles an hour and not sleeping. 

Because the second my mood just... crashed. You know, when it hit that brick wall and I fell into this horrible low period four months ago, the voices just stopped entirely. They just vanished the minute my brain turned to sludge. So, for the last four months, no, I haven't heard them at all. It's just been completely quiet... well, quiet except for my own terrible thoughts telling me I'm a burden, but no actual whispering voices from outside my head like before. It's almost like my brain was moving so fast back then that it was generating sound, and now it's moving so slow it can't even... I don't know, it's just completely dead now. But yeah, the whispering was only during that one really fast period before the crash.
Did you experience any periods over the last four months where you felt abnormally happy or irritable?

In the last four months? No, no, definitely not. Like I was just saying, these last four months have been completely flat, just that heavy, awful sludge every single day without a single break. But... well, if you mean that time right *before* the crash, you know, when I was doing all those extra shifts and my brain was plugged into the wall socket? Then, yeah. Absolutely. 

It was... it was really intense. For a while during that stretch, I felt almost unstoppable. Like, extra cheerful, you know? I’d be standing there at the register and I felt like I could take on a line wrapping all the way around the store by myself. I was talking to all the customers, cracking jokes, bagging things at lightning speed, just feeling so incredibly good, like absolutely nothing could bring me down. I really thought I was just having the best week of my life and showing the managers exactly why I deserved that shift lead spot. 

But the weird thing was... it wouldn't always stay happy. It was like this switch would just flip out of nowhere, and I would get so, so incredibly agitated. I’d snap hard over the smallest, most ridiculous things. Like, I remember one time my manager came over and just asked me to count my drawer again at the end of my shift—which is a totally normal thing, right? They do it all the time if the computer thinks something is even a penny off or if they're just doing an audit. Normally I wouldn't care, I'd just count the drawer. But right then? I just completely lost it. I snapped at him so hard, my heart was racing, and I was just furious that he would even ask me to do it.
